note: Seed 303 stood 88 s at a wall in v2 because the lookahead lost ground contact whenever the reported ya was 0. A jump pressed now always failed in the simulation, so the plan to jump at the next decision won every time. Seed 101 died in v2 because the jump was put off to the next decision, which scored 0.4 higher, and that input landed a tick late. The unkept version fixed both, but its new rule made Mario jump as soon as any jump was safe. On seed 101 that meant a jump 1.6 tiles worse, straight into a wall. It also only replayed inputs one tick late, and its fatal press just before landing failed because the input came a tick early. Starting from v2, I keep the ground-contact fix and the check that a plan never jumps at a decision where jumpKey would be wait. Every plan is now replayed with the input one tick early and one tick late, and a plan counts only if it survives as many timings as the best allowed action does. Mario jumps now only when that is within 0.5 of a plan that needs its jump at the next decision. A new stuck flag (on the ground without moving for about 0.4 s) makes Mario take any safe jump, so no tie between rules can hold him at a wall for the rest of the game.

instructions:
Play the game well. Infinite Mario. Left and Right walk, S jumps (hold it for a higher jump), A runs (and throws fireballs with the fire flower), Down ducks. Run to the right through the level as far as you can: jump over pits and obstacles, stomp enemies by landing on them from above (touching one any other way hurts, and small Mario dies of it), avoid piranha plants and bullets. Reaching the end of the level wins it.
jumpKey tells what pressing S (the actions jump, jumpRight, runJumpRight) does now: start = on the ground, a jump starts; boost = rising in a jump that holding S still lifts; landing = in the air but touching down just before the press takes effect, so the press starts a jump right on landing; wait = pressing S now starts nothing, and holding it would block the next jump.
stuck = true when Mario has stood on the ground without moving for about 0.4 s.
outcome[action] is a physics lookahead of about 0.9 s after the input lag. The action is held for one decision, then Mario keeps that direction and keeps S held while a jump still lifts. Mario may also start one more jump at a later decision, but only at a decision where S could start a jump; the best of those plans is reported. The real input delay varies by about one game tick, so every plan is replayed with the input landing on the expected tick, one tick earlier and one tick later. Allowed actions are all actions except the jump actions when jumpKey is wait. When an allowed action has a plan that survives more of these timings, a plan counts only if it survives as many, and a plan that fails one of them is reported with that failure. fate: safe; stomp (lands on an enemy, which is fine); hurt (touches an enemy, piranha or bullet, and small Mario dies); pit (falls to death). t = ms until the harm when no plan avoids it. gain = tiles ahead of Mario's current position, averaged over the lookahead, so more progress made sooner scores higher. hop (non-jump actions only) = when that plan must start its jump: none, next (at the very next decision) or later.
Rules. When status is none, press jump or idle (equally good). When it is dying or won, idle. Otherwise:
1. When jumpKey is wait, never choose jump, jumpRight or runJumpRight.
2. Keep the remaining actions whose fate is safe or stomp. If there are none, take the remaining action with the largest t, counting a hurt as 5000 ms later when big is true (big Mario survives a hit); actions within 20 ms of it are equally good.
3. When jumpKey is boost and a jump action is kept, keep only the jump actions (finish the jump).
4. Let best be the highest gain among the kept actions. When jumpKey is start or landing: a) if stuck is false and a kept non-jump action with hop none or later has a gain within 0.3 of best, keep only those non-jump actions, so Mario jumps only when it helps; b) otherwise, if a kept jump action has a gain within 0.5 of best (or any kept jump action when stuck is true), keep only those jump actions: a jump needed by the next decision is made now unless waiting is clearly better, and a Mario stuck in place jumps; c) otherwise keep the actions within 0.3 of best. For any other jumpKey keep the actions within 0.3 of best.
5. Take the highest gain among those left; actions within 0.1 of it are equally good.
threat (nearest danger), pitAhead/pitWidth and wallAhead/wallHeight (tiles from Mario's front when the input lands; a pitAhead of 0 or less means the front is already over the pit) tell what the outcomes are reacting to.
